name: Missing function-level authorization on a privileged endpoint
requires: a low-privilege authenticated session and the ability to observe an admin or staff surface
at least one privileged endpoint whose path, method, or payload shape can be identified
an anonymous baseline to distinguish authentication failure from authorization failure
questions: Which privileged endpoints exist, and is the role check enforced in the handler, in shared middleware on that route group, or only in the client that hides the menu item?
When called with a low-privilege session, does the endpoint return 200 with privileged data, or 401 and 403 that indicate a real gate?
Does the anonymous call fail with 401 while the low-privilege call succeeds, isolating authorization from authentication?
Is the role or permission read from a token claim, a session record, or a request field the caller can set?
Does a method or path variant reach the same handler without the guard, such as PATCH instead of PUT, or a trailing slash, or a different API version prefix?
Are administrative operations exposed as separate actions on an otherwise authorized endpoint, selected by a body field rather than a distinct route?
Does a lower role reach a superset of another role's permissions through a role hierarchy, an impersonation feature, or a support-mode header?
Is the guard applied to the collection route but omitted on the per-item route, or the reverse?
false_positives: The endpoint returns 403 for the low-privilege session, which is the authorization working rather than failing
The low-privilege session was actually issued an admin-equivalent role by the test setup, so the comparison was never unprivileged
The data returned is public information that the same low-privilege user can already see in the normal UI
The anonymous request returned 200 but with a login page body, which is a redirect or SPA shell rather than protected data
The endpoint is a stub or feature-flagged off for everyone, so its reachability does not depend on the caller's role
The privileged action succeeded but was recorded and reverted, or applied only to the caller's own records
poc_must_show: the privileged endpoint and the exact request issued with the low-privilege session's credential
the response body showing data or an effect that the UI and role model deny to that session
the anonymous call to the same endpoint returning 401 or 403, isolating authorization from authentication
the same request with a genuinely privileged session, so the delta is the role and nothing else
for a state-changing claim, the resulting privileged state observed from the privileged session afterwards
impact_bar: a low-privilege session successfully invokes a privileged function or retrieves data the role model denies, with anonymous and privileged baselines both shown
